dct_description_sm: The research project focuses on Arctic marine microbes, especially planktonic microorganisms (phytoplankton and other protists and bacteria). The overall project addresses questions as:  How many micro-organisms are in the water column? What is their genetic and metabolic diversity? Which factors determine growth and mortality? An important goal of the project is to understand the role of biodiversity in ecosystem function, for example, carbon budgets and food availability to higher trophic levels that inhabit both pelagos and benthic marine environments.  The project addresses very significant knowledge gaps and establishes baseline information on taxonomic makeup and ecological distribution of microbes in the ocean. Because the Arctic has opened up, more research vessels have been collecting suitable samples for DNA analysis in the Arctic to construct phylogenic diversity and distribution maps of phytoplankton, other protists and bacteria in the pan-Arctic Ocean.
dct_title_s: Pan-Arctic microbial survey revealed by high-throughput sequencing
